## English Translation on Project Gutenberg

The memoirs have been translated by Arthur Machen and are available on Project Gutenberg (eBook No. 2981). This is "The Rare Unabridged London Edition Of 1894 Translated By Arthur Machen".

## Public Domain Status

The work is in the public domain in the United States, meaning no one owns a United States copyright in these works, so copies can be distributed without permission and without paying copyright royalties.

## Translation History

It's worth noting that Arthur Machen's English translation, published in 1894, used one of the inaccurate censored versions and remained the standard English edition for many years. A previous bowdlerized version was originally known in English as "The Memoirs of Jacques Casanova," and the unexpurgated English translation was published between 1966 and 1971.

The Project Gutenberg edition provides free access to this classic work of memoir and autobiography.

This anonymous memoir was privately published in 1888 as a 4,000 page, originally eleven volume work featuring detailed accounts of one man ("Walter")'s experiences with sex and sexuality.

The full text is available through multiple sources:

3. **GitHub (GITenberg)** - The book is available as a public domain repository on GitHub.

The work was published anonymously by Amsterdam-based Auguste Brancart and has been widely banned as "smut" or "erotica". The work is in the public domain in the United States because it was published before January 1, 1931.

You can access the full text directly through Project Gutenberg or Internet Archive using the links found in the search results above.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Internet Archive and copyright status:

**General Copyright Framework:**

When the term of copyright for a work expires, it falls into the public domain and loses all copyright protection, allowing works in the public domain to be freely copied in whole or in part. The copyright term depends on when a work was written or published—before 1978, copyright lasted 28 years with optional renewal for another 28 years, but after 1978, the term is the lifetime of the author plus 50 years.

**Internet Archive's Copyright Policy:**

The Internet Archive does not make guarantees as to the copyright status of items on archive.org and cannot guarantee information posted on item details regarding copyright or other intellectual property rights. The Internet Archive has no special immunity to copyright law, and while people upload illegal content, it is the content owner who has to file the takedown request.

**"Free to Read" vs. Public Domain:**

The search results don't specifically address the distinction between items marked as "free to read" versus items that are in the public domain. However, uploaders can provide information about use rights either directly in the description or by selecting a Creative Commons license, which will be viewable via a logo on the details page. This suggests that "free to read" might indicate restricted licensing rather than true public domain status.

If you need more specific information about erotic fiction collections on the Internet Archive, I'd recommend searching their site directly or reviewing individual item pages for copyright status.

The Public Domain Review is an online journal and not-for-profit project dedicated to the exploration of curious and compelling works from the history of art, literature, and ideas. sources.name: Project Gutenberg — Erotic Fiction bookshelf (#33)
sources.legalStatus: Verified Public Domain in US. Project Gutenberg's standard PG license header is authoritative — every title carries an explicit PD declaration. Note: PD-in-US ≠ PD globally; some titles still under copyright in EU/UK.
sources.approximateRelevantVolume: ~16 titles total in the dedicated Erotic Fiction bookshelf, of which only ~10-12 are literary erotica (the rest are reference/manuals like Kama Sutra, or non-English). Realistically 5-8 English-language literary-erotica titles usable: Fanny Hill (1748), Venus in Furs (1870), Decameron (1350s, 2 vols), Erotica Romana / Roman Elegies (Goethe, late 1700s), Aline et Valcour (Sade, French only).
sources.era: Almost entirely pre-1900. Oldest: Petronius's Satyricon (1st century CE) and Decameron (14th century). Most recent: Ulysses (1922, modernist — borderline). Median is mid-1700s to late-1800s.
sources.voiceFit: Brutally honest: BAD fit for a modern slow-burn literary-erotica site. Fanny Hill's voice — 'I was now reduced to such a state of distress... that the velvet-soft pressure of his glowing instrument...' — is florid 18th-century euphemism. Venus in Furs is German philosophical-fetishist 1870s prose. Decameron is medieval frame-narrative bawdy. NONE of these read as contemporary literary-erotica voice (think Garth Greenwell, Mary Gaitskill, Melissa Febos). Use as historical curiosity only — never as a default sample for a contemporary site.
sources.tagFit: Poor. A 591-tag modern taxonomy almost certainly includes tags like 'consent-forward,' 'queer contemporary,' 'praise kink,' 'aftercare,' 'dom/sub dynamics with modern negotiation,' 'monogamish,' etc. The PG corpus pre-dates the entire vocabulary of modern kink-and-consent discourse. Tags that would map: gender-coded acts, fetish (Sacher-Masoch → masochism literally), maybe orientalist exotica. Tags that would NOT map: anything post-1970s sexual-politics vocabulary, anything queer-affirming, anything with modern consent framing. You'd be force-fitting.

input.modernPDExists: No. There is no usable pool of CC0 or verified-public-domain MODERN erotic fiction online. After surveying Creative Commons indexes, Project Gutenberg post-1929 holdings, Standard Ebooks, Wikisource, Internet Archive, and Public Domain Review, the available verified-PD corpus is overwhelmingly pre-1930 (most of it pre-1900), with voice and tag vocabularies that do not match a contemporary literary-erotica site. Contemporary authors essentially never release erotica under CC0 — the genre's economics (paid platforms, Patreon, indie publishing) and stigma both push the opposite direction. The 'modern free erotica' that exists online is either (a) author-promo content still under copyright, (b) Controlled-Digital-Lending material on IA that is legally contested and NOT public domain, or (c) unlicensed/pirated. None of these are safe as fixture sources.
input.overallVerdict: PD content is NOT a viable path for Lucifer's Diary fixtures if the goal is voice-representative test data. The honest landscape: roughly 15-25 unique English-language literary-erotica works are reliably PD (Fanny Hill, Venus in Furs, Decameron, Casanova/Machen, Teleny, The Pearl, Romance of Lust, My Secret Life, Sade selections, Frank Harris, Autobiography of a Flea, plus a handful of erotic poetry — Sappho, Catullus, Goethe's Roman Elegies). Every single one is pre-1930, most are Victorian or earlier, and they share three disqualifying traits for a modern slow-burn-literary-erotica fixture pool: (1) florid period-specific euphemism that reads as parody to contemporary eyes, (2) consent and sexual-politics vocabularies that are absent or actively offensive (colonial fetish, racism, non-consent framed as titillation), and (3) tag-taxonomy mismatch — a 591-tag modern system built around contemporary kink/identity/consent discourse cannot meaningfully tag Victorian clandestine prose without force-fitting. Three practical paths forward, ranked: (1) BEST: commission a small (~20-50 piece) original fixture corpus from a freelance erotica writer with a work-for-hire / CC0 release — gives voice fidelity, tag fidelity, and unambiguous license. (2) ACCEPTABLE: generate synthetic fixture text with an LLM specifically for fixture-display purposes (clearly labeled as synthetic, not as real content). (3) WORST but cheapest: use the PG corpus for STRUCTURAL fixtures only (chapter counts, word counts, tag density) without ever surfacing the actual prose in UI. Do NOT mix Victorian PD prose into anything a real user would see — it will undermine the contemporary brand. The Standard Ebooks 'we curate PD with editorial polish' model is not a shortcut here because they correctly don't curate erotica. Internet Archive's 'free to read' is a copyright trap, not a source. CC0 modern erotica is essentially a null set.
